jobs.title: Electrical Engineer
jobs.description_text:
Lexington Medical, Inc. is hiring an Electrical Engineer in Bedford, MA to design and develop embedded electrical systems for our AEON™ surgical stapling platform. As an Electrical Engineer at Lexington Medical, you will work hands-on across the hardware development lifecycle, from circuit design and PCB development through prototyping, testing, debugging, verification, and production. 

About Lexington Medical

jobs.title: Embedded Software Engineer
jobs.description_text:
As an Embedded Software Engineer at Lexington Medical, you will write and debug the firmware that drives a surgical stapler, C and C++ on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers controlling the motors, sensors, and mechanisms inside the device. This is an early-career role for an engineer who has already done real embedded work in an internship or co-op and wants to keep building hardware-driven products rather than move away from the hardware. Because the electrical and mechanical engineers who designed the board and the mechanism sit in the same building in Bedford, you debug at the bench with the people who can change either one.

About Lexington Medical

Lexington Medical is a medical device company designing and manufacturing surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our AEON™ Endostapler is an FDA-cleared, minimally invasive surgical stapler used in operating rooms around the world. With engineering, manufacturing, and quality working closely together, engineers stay close to the product and see their work move from an idea through prototyping, testing, manufacturing, and ultimately into the operating room.

jobs.title: Manufacturing Automation Engineer
jobs.description_text:
As a Manufacturing Automation Engineer at Lexington Medical, you will design the fixtures and specify the robotics and automation equipment that build a surgical stapler, then scale those processes as production volume grows. This is an entry-level role built for an engineer coming out of school, and the work is real from the start: the fixture you design gets installed on a line that is running, and you will be on the floor when it does. Manufacturing, engineering, and quality all work in the same building in Bedford, so the loop between designing something and finding out whether it worked is short. 

About Lexington Medical 

Lexington Medical designs and manufactures AEON™ surgical stapling technology at our headquarters in Bedford, Massachusetts, just outside Boston. Our products are used in minimally invasive surgery, where precision, reliability, and quality matter every time. Because engineering, manufacturing, and quality work together under one roof, the people building and supporting our products are close to both the process and the decisions behind it.

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Co-Op
jobs.description_text:
As a Mechanical Engineering Co-Op at Lexington Medical, you will design, test, and document parts for the AEON surgical stapler. This is a six-month, full-time co-op on our engineering team in Bedford, Massachusetts, and the projects are real ones: components going into a product used in operating rooms, and processes running on our own production floor. The work moves from CAD and drawings through fixture builds, testing, and the documentation that has to stand up to regulatory scrutiny, so you finish the term with a clear picture of how a medical device actually gets made. 

About Lexington Medical

About the Role

jobs.title: Mechanical Engineering Manager

As a Mechanical Engineering Manager at Lexington Medical, you will lead a team of mechanical and product engineers designing surgical staplers from concept to production. You will help shape how the team plans, reviews, and delivers its work while staying close to the engineering itself. The instruments your team designs move from CAD and bench testing into operating rooms, and you will own that path from the first requirements to the Design History File.

This is a hands-on, systems-level role. You will be in the lab working directly with hardware, not reviewing spec sheets. You will also shape the evaluation methodology and the tooling behind it, so each platform assessment runs faster and more consistently than the last.

What You'll Be Building

  • Own end-to-end evaluation of assigned platforms, from test plan to benchmark report

jobs.description_text:
Your Impact at LILA

Our Platform Evaluation team tests and benchmarks alternative robotics platforms, including mobile manipulators, AMRs/AGVs, and other form factors, against our current production baseline. The team builds custom mobile manipulators by combining off-the-shelf components from different AMR and robot arm manufacturers, for example mounting one or more arms from a given vendor onto an AMR base from another.

As the Robotics Mechanical Design Engineer, you will own the mechanical design of these custom configurations end to end: mocking up multiple iterations (different arm brands, mounting positions, and configurations), modeling them fully in CAD, and preparing designs for simulation and physical build.

You will work closely with the Platform Evaluation engineers, who validate designs in simulation (NVIDIA Isaac Sim) and in physical testing once built. This is a hands-on mechanical and mechatronic design role, not a robotics software or controls position.

What You'll Be Building

  • Design and iterate mounting and integration concepts combining robot arms with AMR/AGV base platforms
  • Produce multiple design options per platform combination for evaluation
  • Model custom mobile manipulator configurations in CAD, including brackets, structural supports, and interface hardware
  • Run mass, center-of-gravity, and payload analysis to keep configurations within manufacturer
